_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_as_of: 2026-08-27 (afternoon) · Sam ruled that the funding model is a DRAFT: a piece of data we do not have yet is not a reason to stop and not a fault in the design — build the mechanism and let the figure read zero until the data arrives. That reverses an earlier call that the noncredit work was blocked. One edge he drew in the same breath decides everything: a BLANK is fine, a number that is quietly WRONG while looking right is not. He also reported six things from using the tab — two are simply not built yet (he is ahead of us), two are real bugs in signing in and unlocking, and two are accessibility checks we have not run on the funding tab or the site header. items.text: The Title 5 55050 package is ready to send: v5 of the Word file, with every one of your decisions in it and real tracked changes against the version the Board of Governors adopted, plus a Regulatory Action Proposal in the same format as your November one. Undoing every tracked change gives back the adopted regulation word for word, checked by machine. The only blank left is the 2026-27 calendar — five steps to set dates against: the curriculum committee, field vetting, Consultation Council, and two Board readings.

One judgment call left on the package: whether the four policy items from your November draft travel with it or separately. Recommendation is separately — they were argued last November and lost, and bundling lets a reader treat the whole filing as reopening a settled negotiation. Two notes: the new grading clause needs its companion amendment to section 55023, which is what makes a 'credit' mark exist at all; and the no-fee item just gained a second legal anchor, because the Career Passport statute says a student's records must be available at no or low cost.

Three quick fixes on the policy register, now that the draft is settled. Entry #16 points at the wrong lettered paragraph — the August adoption moved that clause. Entry #2 still asks the Legislature for reciprocity between colleges, which is already law; what survives is the 'no second review' half and the CSU/UC half. And entry #10 deserves a fresh look now that #9 is settled: recording the credit was never the same request as flagging where it came from.

The bigger one when you have time. Entry #7 — getting prior-learning credit to generate funding — names the Department of Finance and the attendance rules as its obstacle. A section of the same new bill sets up a workgroup that must design exactly that kind of non-seat-time funding measure and report it to Finance by October 2028. It is scoped to competency-based education rather than prior learning, so it is a venue rather than a solution, but it is the room where this gets designed and we are not in it yet.

Separate from the regulation and probably bigger. The new law makes every dollar of implementation funding conditional on 'the metrics described in paragraph (1)' — and paragraph (1) describes four goals and supplies no metrics at all. Somebody has to define them, and the Implementation Funding model is the only college-by-college quantification of those goals that exists. It already covers access and completion, and the pilot-project one is satisfied because MAP is named in the statute. Career advancement is the gap you said you would cover through CPL Projects and the Credential Registry. This needs no rulemaking, which is exactly its advantage — keep it out of the amendment conversation.

The memory entries are now readable end to end in plain English — 202 were rewritten, and there are no entries left without plain text, none with developer jargon, and no British spellings. The hopper of unreviewed entries is worth an afternoon whenever you have one. Two small things still need you: one entry is marked stale but still carries a verification stamp, which needs your go to clear, and 26 verified entries do not name who verified them.

The nightly load of the MAP custom reports failed: MAP returned the student-details dataset twice and left out the exhibit-by-catalog-year one entirely, so the run stopped rather than publishing a partial picture — which is the gate working. Needs a look at whether the report itself was renamed on MAP's side.

Sierra ran out of API credit this evening and you restored it — thank you. That is the third time (21 Aug, 22 Aug, 25 Aug). The uptime monitor did its job and raised the alert, but it only looks every three hours, so an outage can run that long before anyone is told. A balance-threshold alert on the Anthropic account itself would catch it before it becomes an outage, and that is the one thing a monitor here cannot do.

Sierra is running on Haiku 4.5 as the temporary cost measure you asked for — about a third the price of what it was on (Sonnet, not Opus). When corporate billing is released, switching back needs no code change and no session: set CPL_CHAT_MODEL on the Supabase project to claude-sonnet-4-6. Worth trying the whole-register sweep on Haiku once before you rely on it — a sixteen-row legal analysis is the hardest thing the assistant does, and it is where a smaller model would show first.

Settled, and noted so nobody undoes it: the automated check found 40 of 41 answers still correct on Haiku, and the one it dropped was the caveat beside the big waiting-credit number — the reminder that roughly a third of reviewed credit is correctly ruled Not Applicable, so the total is a ceiling rather than a debt. You said you can live with it for now, so it stays as it is. The fix is written down and ready if you change your mind: move that caveat next to the number itself instead of into a rules list further away, which would make it stick on any model.

for_sam.title: Decide the noncredit minimum award
for_sam.note: At $50,000, 30 of the 33 noncredit institutions sit exactly on the minimum and growth does not start paying until 3,909 FTES — which is the opposite of the incentive you wanted. At $15,000 nobody is on the minimum and growth pays from 384 FTES. $60,000 is not affordable at all. Opening it to every noncredit institution does not work at this pot: even at full parity it buys about $16,000 each.

for_sam.title: Remove "noncredit mirror courses" from the credit lane's strategy list when noncredit goes live
for_sam.note: Priority 3 currently invites colleges to bank noncredit work under the credit lane. Today that is not double-counting, it is single-counting in the wrong lane — which is the stepchild problem itself.

for_sam.title: Watch for ITPI on the origination ID
for_sam.note: Pedro has the request and says it will take longer than tonight's fix. The one question only they can answer: can a college have a SECOND, noncredit landing page with its own ID, or is that only available to standalone institutions like North Orange and San Diego Continuing Education? That decides whether this reaches about 108 colleges or just a handful.

for_sam.title: Open the Fact Sheet and the Sierra / veteran-map pages on your phone
for_sam.note: Both were audited and fixed, and no session can check them — the sandbox cannot reach the live site. This is the only step left on either, which is why both moved out of the always-loaded notes today.

for_sam.title: One memory row still carries a false verification stamp
for_sam.note: Marked stale and verified by 'curator' at the same time. Awaiting your go. The eleven rows verified by you or Jenni are real attribution and must never be swept.

for_fable.title: Give a priority an explicit data source, then build the noncredit lane
for_fable.note: FIRST, but no longer a blocker. The model works out which data to measure a priority against by matching words in the priority's own text, and all three noncredit metrics match the CREDIT data. That is not a missing number — it is a wrong one that looks right, which is the one thing Sam's draft-model ruling does not permit. Then: noncredit earns, then the display.

for_fable.title: Sign-in email box cannot be clicked into — only reached by tab
for_fable.note: Sam hit this. Clicking fails but tabbing works, which is the signature of the box being rebuilt underneath the pointer. There is a strong clue in the code: someone already noticed this and preserved what you had TYPED across the rebuild, but not where the cursor was.

for_fable.title: The unlock control on the funding tab does not respond
for_fable.note: Sam guessed it was because that tab does not use the team phrase. It does — so this is a real defect, not expected behavior. Two leads are noted in the handoff.

for_fable.title: Accessibility and mobile check: the funding tab and the COBI header
for_fable.note: The header behaves oddly on zoom. Reuse the pattern we already have for the public pages — one check that runs in the test suite, and a separate browser-driven one for anything to do with layout, because the test suite cannot see layout at all.

for_fable.title: Read the manually-started MAP load, and watch whether the schedule fires tomorrow
for_fable.note: Today's did not start on time so it was kicked off by hand. If it fails, the log now carries MAP's own words for each report — read those rather than guessing.
